subject: maths

concepts.title: Circumference of a Circle
concepts.definition: Stretch a string once around a round curve and its length equals the width across times the unchanging number pi.
concepts.key_idea: Around-over-across never changes: the ratio is pi.
question_patterns: Calculate the round-trip length of a circle with radius 7 cm.
What length of rope wraps once around a wheel of diameter 21 cm?
How far does a wheel of radius 35 cm travel in one rotation?
Find the walking distance around a circular track of radius 70 m.
State the boundary length of a circle whose radius is 10 cm.

solution_steps.explain: Twice pi times the radius gives the length around.

solution_steps.action: Use the diameter if the radius is unknown
solution_steps.explain: Since the diameter is twice the radius, the boundary length can also be found as pi times the diameter.
The ratio of the boundary length to the diameter is always the unchanging number pi, which is why the formula holds for every circle.

concepts.title: Area of a Triangle (Heron's Formula)
concepts.definition: Know just the three side lengths; the area follows from the half-sum trick.
concepts.formula: area = sqrt(s * (s - a) * (s - b) * (s - c)) where s = (a + b + c) / 2
concepts.key_idea: Half the outline sum, scaled by its drops to each side, then rooted.
question_patterns: Find the area of a triangle with sides 8 cm, 11 cm and perimeter 32 cm.
A triangular plot has sides in the ratio 3:5:7 and perimeter 300 m; calculate its area.
Compute the area of the triangle whose sides are 18, 24 and 30.
Work out the area of a triangle with sides 5, 12 and 13.
Use the half-sum method for sides 7, 8 and 9.

solution_steps.explain: s is half the sum of sides a, b, c.
Take the root of s times its drops to each side.
Each drop (s - a), (s - b), (s - c) must be positive, which is guaranteed when the three sides satisfy the triangle inequality; this confirms the area is real.

concepts.title: Area of a Circle
concepts.definition: The covering of a round disc measures pi times radius times radius.
question_patterns: Calculate the disc covering from area = pi x radius x radius for radius 14 cm.
Calculate the lawn area of a circular garden of diameter 28 m.
How much metal goes into a disc of radius 10 cm?
What space does a rug of radius 3.5 m cover?
Compute the covered area for radius 21 cm.

solution_steps.explain: Pi times radius squared gives the covering.

solution_steps.action: Use the diameter if the radius is unknown
solution_steps.explain: Since radius is half the diameter, the area can also be written as one-quarter of pi times the diameter squared.

solution_steps.action: Relate area to the boundary length
solution_steps.explain: The area can also be found from the boundary length as radius times boundary over two, since the boundary length is twice pi times radius.

concepts.title: Area of a Sector
concepts.definition: A wedge cut out by two radii carries a share of the disc set by its corner at the middle.
concepts.key_idea: The wedge's share equals its corner's share of a full turn, times the whole disc.
question_patterns: Find the area of a sector with radius 7 cm and angle 60 degrees.
Calculate the quadrant area when the boundary around is 44 cm.
What area does a clock hand of length 14 cm sweep in 30 minutes?
Compute a minor sector's area for angle 90 and radius 10.
Work out the sector area for angle 120 on a 6 cm disc.

solution_steps.action: Take the corner's share of the disc
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the whole disc by theta over 360.

solution_steps.action: Find the full disc area first
solution_steps.explain: Compute pi times radius squared to get the area of the entire circle before taking the sector's share.

solution_steps.action: Confirm the angle fraction is valid
solution_steps.explain: The angle theta must lie between 0 and 360 degrees so that the share theta over 360 is a proper fraction of the whole disc, giving a meaningful sector area.

concepts.title: Brahmagupta's Formula
concepts.definition: For a four-sided shape pinned on a curve, the area comes from the four sides alone through the half-sum drops.
concepts.formula: area = sqrt((s - a) * (s - b) * (s - c) * (s - d)) where s = (a + b + c + d) / 2
concepts.key_idea: Sides alone fix the area once the shape sits on a curve.
question_patterns: Find the area of the curve-pinned four-sided shape with sides 5, 5, 12 and 12.
Calculate the area for sides 3, 4, 5 and 6 pinned on a curve.
Compute the area from sides 7, 8, 9 and 10.
Work out the area of the pinned shape with equal sides 10, 10, 10 and 10.
Use the four-side half-sum method for sides 12, 16, 21 and 9.

solution_steps.explain: s is half the sum of sides a, b, c, d.
Root the product of s minus each side.
solution_steps.compute: area = sqrt((s - a) * (s - b) * (s - c) * (s - d))

solution_steps.explain: Brahmagupta's formula applies only to four-sided shapes pinned on a curve, so verifying that the quadrilateral is cyclic ensures the area result is valid.
